extracted.intended_audience: bacterial taxonomists, nomenclature committee members, and culture-collection curators
extracted.subtask_description: Formal Judicial Commission opinions and standards for the naming, conservation, rejection, and typification of bacterial taxa (generic and specific names, family names, and designation of type/neotype strains). Used to decide validity, legitimacy, conservation, rejection, and type designations in prokaryote nomenclature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valid publication of a name
rubrics_metrics.description: A name is 'validly published' only when it meets the publication requirements of the International Code of Nomenclature of Bacteria and Viruses (examples and cases cited). Names published without required elements are not validly published and have no standing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of not validly published: hypothetical genera with no species named; 'temporary' genera established solely as a haven for insufficiently described species; new genera published without naming or identifying the species. If a later author recognizes the generic name and uses it with a specific epithet for the species described by the first author, the generic name may be validated and the species name ascribed appropriately — proposals for validation should be submitted to the Judicial Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimacy of a name
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if validly published, a name may be illegitimate (e.g., because it is a later homonym or otherwise contravenes rules). The Commission issues rulings on whether a name is legitimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: names found to be illegitimate were placed on nomina rejicienda or declared without standing; the page cites decisions where valid publication was confirmed and names deemed legitimate (e.g., Shigella dysenteriae).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservation of a specific epithet
rubrics_metrics.description: A specific epithet can be 'conserved' (epitheton specificum conservandum) so that it remains the correct epithet in a species name despite earlier synonyms or competing epithets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: flexneri, boydii, sonnei, typhi, faecalis, rhusiopathiae, meningitidis, phenylpyruvica, sphaeroides, fermentum, fortuitum — conserved against earlier or competing epithets or objective/subjective synonyms; conservation statements explicitly name the epithet and against which epithets it is conserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservation of a generic name
rubrics_metrics.description: A generic name may be placed in the list of conserved generic names (nomina generum conservanda) to preserve its use against competing or earlier names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Escherichia, Staphylococcus, Mycoplasma, Nitrosomonas, Nitrosococcus, Nitrobacter, Chromobacterium (1880), Lactobacillus, Rhodopseudomonas, Agrobacterium, Rhizobium, Moraxella — all explicitly placed in the list of conserved generic names with type species designated where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of generic names and epithets
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic names or specific epithets may be placed in lists of rejected names (nomina generum rejicienda, nomina generum bacteriorum rejicienda, or rejected epithets) and thereby have no standing in nomenclature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons include later homonymy, illegitimacy, nomen dubium or nomen ambiguum, or publication in rejected publications. Examples: Nitromonas (certain usages), Gaffkya, Mima, Herellea, Aerobacter, Cloaca, and many of Trevisan's proposed names placed on rejected lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of family names as conserved (nomina conservanda familiarum)
rubrics_metrics.description: Family-level names may be conserved; the Commission may designate a conserved family name and a type genus for the family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Enterobacteriaceae was placed in the list of conserved family names, with Escherichia designated as the conserved type genus and Escherichia coli as the type species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of type species for a genus
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission designates (or confirms) the nomenclatural type species of a genus when necessary to stabilize nomenclature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: designation or confirmation of type species for genera such as Escherichia (E. coli), Chromobacterium (C. violaceum), Staphylococcus (S. aureus), Selenomonas (S. sputigena), Agrobacterium (A. tumefaciens), Rhizobium (R. leguminosarum), etc.; type attribution may be by original designation or later action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of neotype strains / cultures
rubrics_metrics.description: Where original type material is absent or inadequate, the Commission designates neotype strains (culture strains) as the type for species and records their catalogue numbers and repositories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neotypes are specified with culture collection identifiers (e.g., ATCC, NCTC, NRRL, NCIB). Examples include neotype designations for Vibrio cholerae (ATCC 14035 / NCTC 8021), Chromobacterium violaceum (ATCC 12472 / NCTC 9757), Pseudomonas aeruginosa (ATCC 10145), Streptomyces albus (ATCC 3004/IMRU 3004), Streptococcus agalactiae (NCTC 8181 / ATCC 13813), etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance and deposition of type cultures
rubrics_metrics.description: Type or standard cultures should, as far as possible, be maintained in national Type Culture Collections and in international centers responsible for particular taxa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: for the four Shigella species, type cultures shall be maintained in each national Type Culture Collection and the International Shigella Center (now Centers for Disease Control, Atlanta). Culture collection accession numbers are given in Opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete identification of cultures by appending serotype numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: A culture belonging to certain species may be completely identified by appending the appropriate arabic serotype number to the species name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific instruction applied to Shigella species: append serotype number (arabic) to the species name to fully identify a culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of hypothetical generic names
rubrics_metrics.description: A generic name proposed without names or descriptions of included species (a 'hypothetical' genus) is not validly published and is to be placed in nomina rejicienda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such names have no standing because the genus existence is predicated upon future discoveries; they are specifically listed as not validly published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of 'temporary' generic names
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic names proposed solely as temporary havens for insufficiently described species are not validly published and may be placed in nomina rejicienda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A name proposed with the sole function of being a temporary generic haven is to be regarded as not validly published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic names published without binary combinations may still be valid
rubrics_metrics.description: A generic name published to include previously described and named species, but without simultaneous publication of binary combinations, may still be regarded as validly published if the publication cites previously and effectively published descriptions of a species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such cases the published generic name is regarded as validly published and the consequent combinationes novae are ascribed likewise to the author of the generic name (example described in Opinions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation by later author recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: If a later author recognizes an earlier-published generic name and uses it with a specific epithet to name the species described by the first author, and there has been later general acceptance, the original generic name may be validated with the species name ascribed to the later author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals for such validations should be made to the Judicial Commission for appropriate action; the Opinions cite cases where later usage validated names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegitimacy due to homonymy (including cross-kingdom homonyms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Names that are later homonyms of previously established names (including names of genera of protozoa or viruses) are illegitimate in bacteriology and are to be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 24 (new Rule 51b) states that later homonyms of names applied to genera of protozoa are illegitimate in bacteriology; examples include lists of bacterial names rejected because protozoan genera had priority. The Opinions list many specific homonym rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomen dubium / nomen ambiguum grounds for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Names regarded as nomen dubium or nomen ambiguum (uncertain or ambiguous application) are placed on lists of rejected names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Leuconostoc citrovorum and Aerobacter liquefaciens were considered nomen dubium/ambiguum and placed on lists of rejected names; Aerobacter as a generic name was treated as nomen ambiguum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of names from specific publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Names proposed in certain historical publications may be declared not validly published and thus have no standing; the Commission maintains a list of Rejected Publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: publications by Trécul, Hallier, Billroth, and Ogston were listed; names appearing in those works were judged in many cases not validly published and are included in the Rejected Publications list per Code provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservation against objective and subjective synonyms
rubrics_metrics.description: When conserving a generic name or specific epithet, the conservation may be declared against earlier objective synonyms (same type) and/or against subjective synonyms (different interpretations), thereby stabilizing current usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate conservation of names like Lactobacillus against objective synonyms, and conservation of epithets (e.g., fortuitum, fermentum) against various earlier epithets or synonyms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and publication format of neotype information
rubrics_metrics.description: When a neotype strain is designated, the Opinion records the strain identifier and the culture collection catalogue numbers where deposited for authoritative reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opinion results routinely report culture collection accession numbers (e.g., NCTC 5735, ATCC 13312, ATCC 14035, NCTC 8021) and repositories to allow unequivocal reference to the neotype.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of rejection on higher-rank names (loss of standing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejection of component names (e.g., genera or specific epithets) can cause associated higher-rank names (tribal, family) to lose standing in nomenclature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: rejection of Mima and Herellea and their epithets resulted in loss of standing of the tribal name Mimeae.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservation of species and genus names by specific institutional actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission's decisions may explicitly instruct placement of names in the appropriate lists (conserved or rejected), designate type species, and identify neotype cultures in specified repositories to effect nomenclatural stability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Opinions are the mechanism by which such conservation/rejection/type designations are made binding; each Result section specifies the formal action (placement in nomina conservanda/rejicienda, designation of type/neotype, etc.).
